A1.justification: Both complete, readable PDFs describe the same injective-flow research. Their main text, equations, figures and appendices support reliable comparison despite the changed title, narrower focus and substantial reorganization.

before.justification: v1 reports original synthetic regression and portfolio experiments, including posterior intervals, solution paths and sparsity analyses in Figures 4–9 and Appendix A.6.

after.justification: v2 retains those experiments and adds spherical density-reconstruction results and a comparison against an MCMC sampler using an analytically known posterior.

M1.justification: v2 drops the separately proposed direct graph-hypersurface flow from v1 Section 3.1, narrowing the presented method family. The retained star-like construction still uses angular bijections, radius padding and spherical-to-Cartesian conversion, with unchanged reverse-KL training and documented architectures.

E1.justification: The regression and portfolio tasks are retained. v2 adds three spherical density targets—a von Mises–Fisher distribution, a 50-component spiral mixture and a sinusoidal checkerboard—and conjugate Dirichlet–multinomial posterior inference. These substantially extend the evaluated scenarios; the newly discussed ecological and geoscientific applications are not themselves evaluated.

E2.justification: v2 introduces the first direct comparison against another inference algorithm: an ad-hoc Metropolis–Hastings sampler with Dirichlet proposals, evaluated against the flow and an analytical posterior in Appendix A.6.4, Figure 9. This substantially extends comparison beyond the retained prior-choice and flow-posterior illustrations. The cited simplex-sampling papers are not separately evaluated baselines.

E3.justification: New protocols include density MSE evaluation over 10,000 samples and conjugate-posterior comparisons at dimensions 15, 30 and 50. The MCMC experiment specifies 1,000 chains with 100,000 samples each, matched runtime and approximately matched memory within 20%. These are added experimental designs; the documented regression generation, architectures and 10-stock, 200-time-step portfolio setting remain unchanged.

E4.justification: Appendix A.6.4 adds checks of sampler performance across dimensions, alternative proposals and fivefold longer sampling time. These provide focused evidence about persistent difficulties with sparse posteriors. The earlier prior-sensitivity, MAP solution-path and portfolio sparsity analyses are retained.

E5.justification: Both versions report 95% posterior intervals; v2 Figure 9 extends this existing reporting practice to another experiment. Neither adds repeated-training-run variability, seed summaries or significance tests. The new MCMC chain and sample counts describe its sampling protocol rather than uncertainty across experimental repetitions.

E6.justification: v2 newly reports density MSEs of 0.013, 0.011 and 0.024 for the three targets in Section 5.1. Figure 9 adds posterior comparisons showing close flow agreement with the analytical reference and discrepancies for the tested MCMC sampler at dimensions 30 and 50. Existing regression and portfolio results are retained, including v1 Figure 9 as v2 Figure 10; these additions are not same-setting improvements over v1.

T1.justification: v1's parametric-hypersurface definition, standalone graph-flow Theorem 1 and its Appendix A.3 proof are removed. Its star-like Theorem 2 survives as v2 Theorem 1 with essentially the same central result. v2 also removes the Sherman–Morrison derivation and changes the stated Gaussian-elimination cost from O(d) to O(d²). Moving spherical-coordinate definitions to the appendix does not constitute new theory.

C1.justification: The abstract, contribution list and conclusion narrow the central claim from parametric hypersurfaces with a separate star-like Cartesian extension to star-like manifolds themselves. Exact, efficient Jacobian evaluation and the Objective Bayesian and simplex-inference applications remain central, with greater emphasis on variational inference from unnormalized targets.

C2.justification: v2 explains the tested MCMC sampler's difficulties through sparse mass near simplex boundaries and discusses target-specific limitations of sampler comparisons. It explicitly qualifies the objective prior as preferable when less information is desired, rather than generally better, and connects the dimensionality limitation to the proof's rank condition. Existing regression and portfolio interpretations remain.

D1.justification: v2 supplies new target specifications, sampler-construction details and computational-budget information. Existing layer configurations, Adam training, RTX2080Ti hardware and the FlowConductor link remain. Conversely, the portfolio reference loses v1's explicit Mendeley dataset identifier, 10.17632/gx66wsgwkr.1, replacing it with a journal citation and making direct data access less explicit.

R1.justification: v2 substantially expands positioning through conformal embedding flows, manifold-distribution literature, geometric accounts of objective priors, and mixing-model and simplex-sampling research. In particular, Ross and Cresswell (2021) are acknowledged as an existing exact, tractable approach under restrictive transformations, qualifying v1's presentation of prior exact methods.

P1.justification: The paper is retitled and Section 3 is reorganized around star-like manifolds and one central theorem. The introduction, background, proof exposition and mixing-model discussion are extensively rewritten; spherical-coordinate definitions move to the appendix. Terminology changes from Bayesian mixture models to probabilistic mixing models, and the application and appendix structures are revised.

P2.justification: v2 changes the document template, title and author layout, headers and heading styles. It removes v1's graph-flow architecture figure, adds the density-reconstruction panels in Figure 3 and the MCMC comparison in Figure 9, and relocates or resizes retained figures with revised captions. The cumulative-return plot is retained as Figure 10 rather than newly added.

improvement.justification: v2 improves empirical checkability through known-target density errors and analytical-posterior comparisons, while clarifying prior-work positioning and applicability qualifications. These strengthen evidence that v1 largely supplied through application illustrations. The gain remains limited: the comparative evidence concerns one ad-hoc sampler, the broader graph-hypersurface result is removed, and direct dataset access becomes less explicit. Overall, the added validation and clearer scope support a modest net quality improvement.
